description: issue #775 (review gate): `wait { name: "ada" }` -- a tick count that is a DICT. Together with its `every` twin `every/every-non-number-record-type-error` (which covers `record`), and with `wait-non-number-list-type-error` / `every-non-number-boolean-type-error` / the turtle pair, this completes `params.actual` across every `OLTypeName` outside `number`/`word`. Before them the whole corpus (`wait`, `every`, `repeat`, `random`) pinned `actual` as only `number` or `word`, so an implementation could report anything at all for a dict and still pass -- confirmed by mutation. `spec/error-model.md` requires an `ol-type` to "name the expected learner concept, such as number, word, list, dict, record, or boolean", so calling a dict a word would violate a MUST. The dict's CONTENTS are genuinely compared: the harness unwraps an `OLDict` runtime value into a plain key->value object before deep-comparing (`tests/conformance/README.md`, "Dict/record contents"), so `params.value` is written here as `{ "name": "ada" }` and an implementation that reported an empty or different dict fails. Needs the Data profile only to CONSTRUCT the value; the check under test is the Interaction one. The `primitive` event is NOT emitted (the pause never runs), only the instruction event precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the argument.

diagnostics.message: wait needs a whole number, but got a dict.
